rationale:
The subject says that, with default features, the crate exposes exactly the listed crate and module items. Each entry gives a Rust item kind and a name within its module. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` carries a {test} reference to it and checks this directly.

- **Generating the real inventory.** The test always runs `cargo doc --locked --offline --no-deps -p trust-but-verify` on the current source tree. It passes no feature flags, so default features apply. It strips the RUSTFLAGS and RUSTDOCFLAGS variables, and it asserts that the command succeeds. `habeas-integration` items are hidden from rustdoc, so they stay outside the compared set, as the text says.
- **Specified side.** `specified_exports` reads the `exports` requirement text from `md/requirements/sdk/public-api.md`. The helper parses every bullet line with a strict regex for kind and name. It asserts that indentation is valid and that no parent is skipped. It requires the root to be a crate and allows only crates and modules to contain entries. It rejects duplicates and an empty list. This yields (path, kind) pairs from the requirement, so both the module path and the item kind are checked.
- **Documented side.** `documented_exports` walks rustdoc's HTML item tables, starting at the crate index and recursing into every `mod` link. It takes the kind from the link class, maps `constant` to `const`, and builds full paths. It panics on unknown categories, so a re-export or other unexpected kind cannot be silently dropped. It also rejects malformed names, non-local links and missing pages, and it rejects duplicates.
- **Exactness.** The test computes both set differences, `missing` and `unexpected`, and asserts that both are empty. A missing item, an extra item, a wrong kind and a wrong module path would each make it fail.

The only text left outside this requirement is that associated methods, fields and variants belong to their types' own contracts. The `habeas-integration` items are also outside the supported interface. Neither needs a test here. The related `sdk_has_no_public_reexports` test is marked for `requirements.sdk.public_api`, not for the subject, so it is not needed for the subject. I found no plausible violation of the exports obligation that these assertions would accept.

text: With its default features, `trust-but-verify` exposes exactly the crate and module
items listed below, following {cite}`requirements.sdk.public_api`. Each entry
states its Rust item kind and its name within the enclosing module. Associated
methods, fields, and variants belong to their types' individual contracts.
The internal `habeas-integration` feature supports Habeas interoperability; its
hidden items are outside this supported interface.
Each public SDK item has one defining module path. The SDK exposes no public
re-exports. Its public modules follow the interfaces introduced in these chapters:
- `domain`: application data and the `Domain`, `NodeContents`, and `SourceNodes` traits.
- `graph`: criterion definitions, graph observations, and evidence; `graph::validator`
- `request`: `ValidationContext`, typed `Ask` builders, context values, and request phases.
- `sources`: project inspection, search queries, and their results.
- `outline`: selectable source contents and language rules; `outline::languages`
supplies bundled languages, and `outline::selector` defines selector syntax.
Source access, search engines, redaction, provider transports, agent-result paging,
and conversation machinery are implementation details of those interfaces.
